message.content:
Hydrogen is the simplest and most abundant element in the universe. Its key properties include:

| Property | Value / Description |
|----------|---------------------|
| **Atomic number** | 1 |
| **Atomic mass** | ~1.008 u (average of isotopes) |
| **Electron configuration** | 1s¹ |
| **Isotopes** | Protium (¹H), Deuterium (²H), Tritium (³H) |
| **Standard state** | Gas at room temperature |
| **Boiling point** | –252.9 °C (20.4 K) |
| **Melting point** | –259.2 °C (14.0 K) |
| **Density** | 0.08988 g/L at STP |
| **Molar volume** | 22.414 L/mol at STP |
| **Reactivity** | Highly flammable; reacts with oxygen to form water (exothermic). Forms hydrides with metals. |
| **Electronegativity** | 2.20 (Pauling scale) |
| **Ionization energy** | 13.598 eV |
| **Bonding** | Forms covalent bonds (H₂), ionic bonds (as H⁺), and metallic bonds (in metal hydrides). |
| **Spectral lines** | Lyman series (UV), Balmer series (visible), Paschen series (IR). |
| **Applications** | Fuel cells, rocket propellant, hydrogenation reactions, medical imaging (MRI contrast agents), etc. |

These properties make hydrogen versatile in chemistry, physics, and engineering.
